back: Problem: damages crops, livestock or property (baboons, bushpigs, elephants raiding fields). Dangerous: threatens human life (lions, crocodiles, buffalo, hippos).
The Communal Areas Management Programme for Indigenous Resources (from 1989): councils and communities manage wildlife on communal land and receive the income.
Nyaminyami (Kariba) and Guruve joined first, in 1989.
Hwange (largest, north-west), Gonarezhou (south-east, Great Limpopo TFP), Mana Pools (Zambezi floodplain, World Heritage Site), Matobo (granite hills, rhinos).
Park: conservation and photographic tourism, no hunting. Safari area: controlled hunting. Conservancy: neighbouring private ranches combined for wildlife.
Settlement near parks and corridors, fields near water, drought pushing animals out, broken fences, growing animal numbers.
Problem animal control, chilli and beehive fences, electric fences, kraaling livestock, land-use planning, compensation, benefit sharing.
Dependence on trophy hunting, international restrictions, money not reaching households, crop losses, habitat loss to settlement.
